newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian workers threaten to shut down oil industry.
newsitem.headline: Colombian workers threaten to shut down oil industry.

text.p: Colombia's main oil workers' union is preparing to "shut down" the state-run oil sector because of the government's refusal to agree on their labour demands, a union leader said Sunday.

Hernando Hernandez declined to say exactly when the 7,000 oil workers union may move to paralyse the refining, production and pumping operations of the state-run oil company Ecopetrol, citing security reasons.

"We are working internally (in the union) for this action which will paralyse production, refining and all other activities because we see the governmment has no real will to negotiate," Hernandez said.

The USO union is already taking a lead role in the nationwide, state workers strike, now in its sixth day but until now it has allowed non-unionized Ecopetrol employees to run operations as part of the company's contigency plans.
The USO's threats to step up strike action come the day before the expiration of a deadline for an agreement between the union and the government on a new collective contract.

USO, known for its combative and fiercely nationalistic stance, is calling for a 30 percent pay hike for its members and an end to what it claims are plans for the creeping privatisation of Ecopetrol.

It has also protested at the arrest of scores of its members on charges of links with the National Liberation Army, Colombia's second largest guerrilla force, which has attacked oil facilities and multinational companies.
